segment.name: A newsletter owner bringing an editor or operations teammate into a formerly solo publishing workflow
segment.organization: A newsletter or small publication transitioning from one owner-operator to a multi-person editorial or operations workflow.
segment.workflow: Draft, review, edit, manage subscribers, and send issues while separating editorial access from billing, API keys, administration, and final sending authority.
segment.need: Role-specific collaboration inside the newsletter system without sharing the owner's credentials or granting every teammate full control.
segment.buyer_role: Newsletter owner, publisher, or content lead
segment.user_role: Editor, proofreader, contributor, or newsletter operations teammate
segment.current_alternative: Google Docs handoffs, emailed drafts, shared credentials, or GitHub pull-request review

reasons: The supplied product truth verifies multi-person management, granular email and sending permissions, immediate revocation, draft review, and an audit trail.
The Turing Way documents an actual multi-person drafting and review workflow using GitHub and HackMD, supporting the underlying need and current workaround.
The source does not establish that The Turing Way bought or used Buttondown Teams, so usage or purchase remains unknown.
Public GitHub newsletter handbooks and repositories are concrete discovery venues for teams with observable review workflows.
unknowns: Whether prospective teams will pay for the Professional plan or the separately stated Teams add-on is unresolved.
The corpus does not show a completed purchase of Buttondown Teams by a formerly solo publisher.
The exact suggestion or tracked-change experience inside Buttondown is not established by the fetched Teams documentation.

evidence.claim: The workflow gathers newsletter contributions from multiple community members through a GitHub issue.
evidence.quote: Create a new GitHub issue where throughout the month you and other community members can suggest news items as a comment.

evidence.claim: GitHub branches, draft pull requests, and WIP labels form an observable external review workaround.
evidence.quote: If working online, please keep the draft mode on for your PR or add “[WIP]” (work in progress) in the title.

evidence.claim: The public GitHub repository and issue workflow provide a concrete venue for identifying collaborative newsletter teams.
evidence.quote: Create a new GitHub issue where throughout the month you and other community members can suggest news items as a comment.

evidence.claim: Buttondown permits immediate access revocation, matching temporary-contributor and contractor workflows.
evidence.quote: Select "Revoke," and your teammate’s permissions will update immediately.

segment.who: Previously solo publishers visibly adding a co-author, editor, proofreader, marketing lead, or operations contractor.
segment.why_them: Public newsletter workflows show multi-person review, fact-checking, image review, and approval before publication. Comparable newsletter tools explicitly separate editor and administrator access, supporting the underlying demand for constrained roles.
segment.trigger: The first collaborator is hired or invited, or a growing publication needs distinct drafting, subscriber-management, and sending responsibilities.
pains: Drafts are copied between Google Docs, email, GitHub, and the sending platform.
Shared credentials expose billing, subscriber data, domains, and API keys.
A reviewer may need to suggest changes without being able to send.
The owner needs to revoke access promptly when a contractor or volunteer leaves.
segment.objection: The pricing page lists Teams at +$79 per month while separate documentation places it on the Professional plan. That unresolved packaging conflict is material, and a small team may continue using free Google Docs or GitHub review instead.
segment.angle: Bring editorial help into the sending workflow while keeping billing, subscriber data, API keys, and the send button under explicit control.
segment.basis: The Turing Way documents a real collaborative process: contributors collect items, draft in GitHub or HackMD, request review, check language and accuracy, approve a pull request, and then publish. This demonstrates the work and the existing handoff alternative, though it does not prove a Buttondown Teams purchase. Buttondown documentation establishes the relevant permissions but leaves plan versus add-on pricing inconsistent.
signals: Newsletter documentation names multiple reviewers or approvers.
Public contributor list shows an editor, proofreader, marketing lead, or operations role.
Drafts are exchanged through Google Docs, HackMD, email, or pull requests before sending.
The organization is recruiting or has recently added a content collaborator.
A security policy discourages shared accounts or requires prompt access revocation.
where: Public editorial handbooks and contributor guides
researchability_reasons: 5 useful observable signals and 5 specific research venues.
The audience is anchored in a concrete workflow or situation.
A clear trigger narrows the evidence to look for.

required_structural_signals.description: At least two people participate in drafting, review, subscriber operations, styling, administration, or sending.

required_workflow_signals.description: The workflow includes editorial review, approval, or a requirement to separate drafting from sending or administration.

optional_signals.description: Drafts are currently reviewed in a separate shared document or repository.
The owner wants collaborators excluded from billing, API keys, domains, or subscriber data.
Some collaborators require temporary or narrowly scoped access.

hard_disqualifiers.description: The buyer requires in-product collaboration but will not consider the published Teams price or a qualifying plan.
The buyer cannot proceed until Buttondown reconciles whether Teams is included in Professional or billed as a separate add-on.

excluded_subsegments: Solo publishers with no review or delegation workflow
Large enterprises requiring a documented support SLA or identity-management features not established here
